messages.author: 9ccdef93cb3041c6
messages.subject: Histogram + xlimits
parts:
Dear all,

I've recently switched to ggplot2 and I must say that, so far, it has
been pretty intuitive.
However, I've encountered some problems when I try to limit the x-
axis.

Taking as an example this histogram:
qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class)

Just pointing out a minor issue, why aren't the bars centred around
its x-axis label? I mean, the "5 cyl" bar is to the right of the x-
axis 5 label, while the "6 cyl" bar is to the left of the label.

- When I try to limit the x-axis:
qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class) +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(5,8))

The x-axis goes from 5 to 8 but I only get the "6 cyl" bar!! Why
aren't the 5 and 8 cyl bars displayed?

- I tried using discrete scales:
qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class) +
scale_x_discrete(limits=c(5,8))

but I get all bars with just the 5 and 8 cyl label!!!!

- Tried stating all labels:
qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class) +
scale_x_discrete(limits=c(5,6,7,8))

but I still get all bars (although with corrected labels)



What do I have to do to have this histogram plotted with just the bars
from 5 to 8??

thanks
FGV

messages.author: 5f8b51633aa2f2a1
messages.subject: Re: Histogram + xlimits
parts:
?xlim()

Just add +xlim(c(5,8)) to the end (and drop the scale_x_*)

HTH,
Michael

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Histogram + xlimits
parts: Hi:

On Fri, Mar 30, 2012 at 2:41 PM, Filipe G Vieira
<fgarret...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear all,
>
> I've recently switched to ggplot2 and I must say that, so far, it has
> been pretty intuitive.
> However, I've encountered some problems when I try to limit the x-
> axis.
>
> Taking as an example this histogram:
> qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class)

Firstly, you're attempting to produce a stacked bar chart but trying
to use the histogram geom to produce it rather than geom_bar().
Secondly, a factor version of cyl would be more effective but you're
trying to fake it by making cyl continuous instead. Evidently, you
want the gap at 7, so one way to produce it is to create a factor
version of cyl whose levels range from 4 to 8 inclusive and then play
around a bit with scale_x_discrete() in conjunction with geom_bar():

mpg$cyl2 <- factor(mpg$cyl, levels = 4:8)
# Fails to insert the gap at 7 since there are no data at 7 (default action)
(p <- qplot(cyl2, geom = 'bar', data = mpg, fill = class))

# This trick using scale_x_discrete() produces the desired gap at 7:
p + scale_x_discrete(limits = as.character(levels(mpg$cyl2)))

# Contrast this with the following (same as first graph above):
p + scale_x_discrete(breaks = levels(mpg$cyl2))

# Equivalent specification:
# p + scale_x_discrete(breaks = as.character(levels(mpg$cyl2)))

There is a subtle but important distinction between limits and breaks
in discrete scales; unfortunately, this distinction is not well
documented at present so it's easy to miss. My first thought was to
use the latter expression, but it elided over cyl = 7 since it
contained no data to plot (this is documented in waiver()); I
serendipitously stumbled over the code I ended up using for the
desired graph.

# To eliminate the level corresponding to 4 cylinders, here is one way:
levels(mpg$cyl2)[-1]
p + scale_x_discrete(limits = as.character(levels(mpg$cyl2)[-1]))

>
> Just pointing out a minor issue, why aren't the bars centred around
> its x-axis label? I mean, the "5 cyl" bar is to the right of the x-
> axis 5 label, while the "6 cyl" bar is to the left of the label.

Because you're using a continuous scale for x and producing a
histogram whose endpoints are not such that the centers of the bins
line up the way you expected. This is why some of the bars are to the
left of a tick mark and others are to the right. The histogram
analogue of stacked bar charts is an area chart, but I doubt that
would look any better in this example or fix the difficulties you're
experiencing.

>
> - When I try to limit the x-axis:
> qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class) +
> scale_x_continuous(limits=c(5,8))
>
> The x-axis goes from 5 to 8 but I only get the "6 cyl" bar!! Why
> aren't the 5 and 8 cyl bars displayed?

Because the limits don't contain the portion of the bar to the left of
5 nor the portion of the bar to the right of 8 in your graph.

>
> - I tried using discrete scales:
> qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class) +
> scale_x_discrete(limits=c(5,8))

As shown above, scale_x_discrete() assumes that the set of potential
values is discrete rather than continuous. You actually get something
out of this code since mpg$cyl is integer, but it should have thrown
an error had mpg$cyl been numeric.

I can sympathize with your angst because learning how to produce
customized positional axis and legend guides is an acquired skill; it
was the part of ggplot2 I had the most trouble getting my head around
when first learning it.

>
> but I get all bars with just the 5 and 8 cyl label!!!!
>
> - Tried stating all labels:
> qplot(cyl,geom='histogram',data=mpg) + aes(fill=class) +
> scale_x_discrete(limits=c(5,6,7,8))
>
> but I still get all bars (although with corrected labels)

Histograms are designed for continuous x scales and bar charts for
discrete x scales (typically factors), but there is some fuzziness in
how they are rendered in ggplot2.

>
>
>
> What do I have to do to have this histogram plotted with just the bars
> from 5 to 8??

I guess the first step would be to recognize the distinction between a
bar chart and a histogram; you want the former in this case.

HTH,
Dennis
